problem:
Change the order of integration in the following integral, 

$$
{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt[3]{2}}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt[3]{2}}{\int }_{{y}^{3}}^{2}f(x,y,z)\,dz\,dy\,dx.
$$

so that it is integrated first with respect to $y,$ then $z,$ then $x.$

activity_context.topic_title: Changing the Order of Integration in Triple Integrals: Changing Region

feedback.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/192cb96645cef0340e99769af3126b9d7e3775ed419e8414e3ad1ed683e919e3.png)

Change the order of integration in the integral

$$
{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2x}{\int }_{0}^{1-x}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x
$$

so that it is integrated first with respect to $x,$ then $z,$ and then $y.$ The integration region $R$ is shown above.
feedback.worked_solution:
We wish to find limits of integration ${u}_{1}(y,z),$ ${u}_{2}(y,z),$ ${v}_{1}(y),$ ${v}_{2}(y),$ $a,$ and $b$ such that

$$
{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2x}{\int }_{0}^{1-x}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(y)}^{{v}_{2}(y)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(y,z)}^{{u}_{2}(y,z)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y.
$$

From the repeated integral, we see that the region of integration $R$ can be written as a type I region as follows:

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,\,0\le y\le 2x,\,\,0\le z\le 1-x}
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x$ to $\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y,$ we write $R$ as a type II region and its projection $D$ onto the $yz$-plane as a type I *plane* region.

To visualize this, imagine firing an arrow through the region parallel to the $x$-axis and in the direction of increasing $x,$ as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/60f61df1520d366f6cbcac0b87e7e5eb453e8f011ff046b29a61cdae41624ddf.png)

The arrow enters the region through the rear boundary and leaves through the front boundary:

- The front boundary of the region, written in the form $x=x(y,z),$ is

$$
z=1-x\,⟹\,x=1-z.
$$

- The rear boundary of the region is

$$
y=2x\,⟹\,x=\frac{y}{2}.
$$

Therefore, the type II representation of $R$ is

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(y,z)\in D,\,\,\frac{y}{2}\le x\le 1-z},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/02bbf0de5dad7ff72970ef5a939ac66fd05dfc06c31a23c37b6204042e1859b8.png)

Now, we consider the projection $D$ as a type I plane region in the $yz$-plane with the top curve given by

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=1-z \\ x=\frac{y}{2}\end{aligned}\,⟹\,\frac{y}{2}=1-z\,⟹\,z=1-\frac{y}{2}.
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/2eea77ae3d1ae7a459dba98c98b20fabbec6b1d3a6cacb718b32688bd4ad11d7.png)

Hence, we have that

$$
D={(y,z)\,:\,0\le y\le 2,\,\,0\le z\le 1-\frac{y}{2}}.
$$

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration so that it is integrated first with respect to $x,$ then $z,$ and then $y,$ we obtain

$$
{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2x}{\int }_{0}^{1-x}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1-y/2}{\int }_{y/2}^{1-z}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y.
$$
